entry.title: Model Hardware Standard: agents get a driver layer for the physical lab
entry.summary: Anthropic's MHS research preview is not a robot and not a new model. It is a shared interface so agents can discover, describe, and operate programmable devices — with the hard problems still sitting in safety, spatial reasoning, and who writes the drivers.

entry.title: Anthropic opens a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard
entry.summary: A shared driver spec for agents to operate programmable lab and factory devices, starting with a closed partner group.

entry.title: Independent write-up: MHS as a common driver layer for physical agents
entry.summary: Ars Technica describes MHS as standardized drivers so agents can talk to arbitrary devices without a custom translator for each instrument.

entry.title: CNBC: Anthropic frames MHS as USB-C for machines, with an industrial follow-on
entry.summary: Business reporting adds competitive context — OpenAI and Amazon hardware spend, Anthropic's silicon hiring — around a still-closed research preview.

entry.title: Hugging Face is adding MHS support in LeRobot
entry.summary: Anthropic names LeRobot as an early adopter for the next phase of device coverage.

entry.title: Raspberry Pi: camera MHS driver tests, broader product integration planned
entry.summary: Another named hardware adopter in the Anthropic preview post, after successful Camera MHS Driver tests.

entry.title: QuEra: agent-written laser lock recovers 99.3% of the time in MHS tests
entry.summary: A partner result from the preview post — specific, quantitative, and still vendor-mediated.
